_effort_doc: ADR-056: per-agent reasoning-effort baseline in subagent_assignments.*.effort, enum {low,medium,high,xhigh,max} (Workflow-native — see docs/ADRs/056-subagent-effort-gradient.md). Deliberately a DIFFERENT vocabulary from session_prefs.model_effort (minimal/fast/balanced/thorough/max), which is a separate session-wide dial this does not touch. Read by skills/foreman/SKILL.md's Dispatch protocol step 2 (prompt-injected directive for bare Agent-tool dispatches, best-effort — the Agent tool has no native effort parameter) and by the same skill's Dynamic-workflows guardrails point 6 (real opts.effort on Workflow's agent() calls, which DOES support it — no separate dispatch/ultracode skill edits were needed, foreman is the single place this convention is documented). escalation_triggers bump the baseline for a specific dispatch when the listed domain_mode is active (first array match wins); matched against stack-config.json's domain_mode (array or bare string, ADR-053). orchestrated_by roles (reviewer, product-critic, red-team, architecture-critic, historian) are NOT structurally parallel despite the shared field: reviewer/product-critic run on routine, high-frequency dispatches where the Claude-side work is thin piping/composition (medium); red-team/architecture-critic are invoked only for high-stakes decisions and must critically assess, not just relay, the cross-family output (high); historian is periodic low-stakes trend summarization (low, same bucket as scribe/librarian).

NOTE: neither gpt-5.5 nor gpt-5.6-terra is covered by the OpenAI free-tier daily quota that triggered this audit (only gpt-5.4-and-earlier is) — this swap is justified purely on benchmark + list-price grounds, not free-tier eligibility. 2026-08-04 propagation-gap fix: this audit's gpt-5.6-terra swap was applied directly to ~/.claude/config/model-routing.json before this repo's own copy was updated to match — backwards from the documented apply-at-SOURCE practice above, and dangerous, since install.sh/update.sh does a plain unconditional overwrite of ~/.claude's copy from source (config/tier-manifests/tier-2.json, no merge flag) and would have silently reverted the live fix on the next stack update. Fixed by syncing source to the already-applied state (commit a4c381e) — do not re-derive this delta from the audit doc, source now matches. Separately, discovered scripts/lib/review-router.sh's rr_config_file() only ever checked <repo>/config/model-routing.json (a per-repo override) and NEVER fell back to ~/.claude/config/model-routing.json (the machine-wide install target) — so every project on the machine except this stack's own source repo silently ignored config entirely and used review-router.sh's hardcoded def values (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, qwen2.5-coder:32b, ...) regardless of what model-routing.json said. Model-routing changes were NOT actually propagating to any other repo before this fix. Fixed via .claude/plans/2026-08-04-review-router-global-fallback.md (Approach A): rr_config_file() now falls back to ~/.claude/config/model-routing.json when no repo-local override exists, before finally falling to the hardcoded default. 3 new regression tests added to tests/test-review-router.sh (section 13); full 48/48 suite passes.
